text:
Sergei Murashov spent most of 2024-25 in the ECHL, stopping pucks for the Wheeling Nailers, and on Wednesday in San Jose he was the best player on the ice. Pittsburgh's goalie turned aside 34 of 36 shots, then watched the Penguins win a shootout, 3-2, over a Sharks team that had erased a two-goal deficit in under five minutes of the third period. Our numbers say he saved about 1.4 goals more than the quality of those shots deserved.

The Sharks' comeback carried two milestones. Macklin Celebrini, the first overall pick in 2024, scored at 11:32 for his 200th career point. Four minutes later Mason Marchment tied it with the 100th goal of his career, set up by Celebrini and Sam Dickinson. Before that, Pittsburgh had led on Samuel Girard's first-period slap shot and Ben Kindel's power-play goal early in the third.

The game was closer than the score suggested. Expected goals, which measure the quality of chances rather than the count of shots, finished 3.39 for San Jose and 3.34 for Pittsburgh, and our simulations gave the Sharks a 51 percent chance to win. Pittsburgh owned the first period, 1.31 to 0.57 in expected goals. San Jose went 0 for 5 on the power play, though those chances were worth 1.27 expected goals, and Yaroslav Askarov stopped 33 of 35 at the other end. The shootout was settled by Kindel's goal in the first round, and the next five shooters were all stopped.

Pittsburgh leaves with the extra point and a goalie worth watching. San Jose gets a point of its own and a night with two milestones to remember.
